I didn't like this game. It looks like an extremely repetitive alpha prototype of The Painkiller. Just 2 arenas with the same monsters where you have to destroy their hordes. Unresponsive controls make you feel like ice skating. You glide. Every miss takes your HP. It's very uncomfortable shooting while moving. All weapons were unlocked after the first fight. I just died because I got bored with ridiculous gameplay and the first song the 20th time on repeat. You can test it if you want to try. But if you read tag "boomer shooter" and thought you could find here something resembling classical DOOM, Unreal or Quake, you've made a mistake. Not a 1% close. The developer did a great job alone. My very best wishes for him. But I can't leave a positive review. I hadn't fun at all.

Harbinger is a wave arena shooter and has good bones but is not fleshed out. The gameplay is very unbalanced yet: You have super fast movement options, but guns' accuracy decreases when you move, so to hit you gotta stand still. This point is intensified by the game punishing you for missing a shot as you lose health when you miss. So you gotta stand still to not miss. This punishment can be turned off but is the intended way of difficulty. With your run, dash, slide you are much faster than the enemies and can easily make a big distance of 30 melee enemy hit reach zones between you and the horde. The maps are big and make this possible. So when you're low on health you can just cheese it: run away, shoot those healing explosions (which respawn) and get back to the enemy horde. This is cheap and could be designed better. The big maps also offer much verticality with higher level paths and jump pads which is pretty cool. It's unfortunate though, that the enemy AI can't really use the jump pads properly. Enemies using the jump pad jump anywhere, but seem not to be able to chase me. They instead take the floor route to a far away ramp to get to me which leaves me threatless for the moment. Also the enemies get stuck on the map under a rock ledge. The movement is good but the camera swaying with every turn feels a bit off. The slide option is not a common slide, but is a toggle option and like sets you on ice skates to slide the whole time, which feels not right. There is a good variety in weapons though switching weapons takes too long, so that staying with one weapon makes more dps than if you switched to another weapon. Switching weapons is rather like that you want a different playstyle now and therefore switch, but not as a reaction of the current situation of the past 2 seconds. The art style is pretty cool, the weapons are punchy and the bones for a good game are all there, just not balanced yet. With some balancing tweaks on the gameplay this one could really shine. Though, currently I can not recommend it.

Literally if Ultrakill and Doom had a baby... this would be it's hellspawn. I downloaded to have something to play while installing something else and ended up playing this longer just to 100% it because I was having such a blast. Very fast paced shooter with a learning curve for each unlock-able gun and taking damage for each shot missed was an interesting concept that was at first frustrating to me, but then added another layer of difficulty I appreciated later. Dialogue was funny and the soundtrack was pretty banger. Pro-tip, unlock the crossbows first as I found myself using these more often than the other weapons pretty much all the time and the reload animation was dope and made you feel like Van Helsing himself. Would love to see what this developer could do with a full length game. Bravo!

"Harbinger" is not to be confused with Harbinger, the 2003 RPG from Dreamcatcher. This is a simple wave survival arena shooter, and despite having no multi-player content, is infected with the EOS malware... now, no online content yet needs online services? Yep, the developer is harvesting telemetry to spy on you. Sometimes if the product is free, YOU are the product. There's no other explanation for the toxic EOS malware to be injected into a Steam game when there's no multiplayer. Not okay, obviously. What do you do in the game? It's wave survival shooting... boring and repetitive immediately. Seriously if this is the kind of experience you want, you could play DooM instead, which is optimised far better and runs rings around this. And DooM has content... waves of samey enemies is not "content". There's a gimmick where you take damage if you miss (what a dumb idea, but you can and should turn it off), this makes the game even less fun to play... but with these kinds of contentless shooters, 5 minutes of gameplay and you've seen the whole thing. The graphics in this game are okayish, obviously inspired by the art style of Valheim, which at least makes the game look more appealing (to some, I guess). And while it's vital for any game to have impressive visuals (gaming is a visual medium, after all), there's more to a game than just the graphics. To be worth a gamers time, the game must match top tier visuals with top tier gameplay, and that's not happening here. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. On pricing and value for gamers, this is only free in a rudimentary sense... the developer has their hand out for a $6 USD "donation" for this as you're expected to buy some extra DLC from Steam... digital panhandling. Like the homeless guys who splash dirty water on your windscreen at the traffic lights. No thanks. Despite having no up-front cost, this failed to appeal to the 120 million+ gamers on Steam. SteamDB showed the game peaked at just a dozen or so concurrent players, and now there's basically nobody playing it. Even though it's free. This is a dismal public reception, but it's easy to see why gamers rejected it. Bearing in mind that free games don't add +1 to your game collector count, should you bother adding this to your library and downloading it? This is a "maybe" experience... if you have a lot of free time on your hands and nothing else to do, why not? But for the purposes of a review, this isn't something I can say everyone must try. It's not quite there. Valve doesn't give us a "maybe" option in reviews, but if they did, that's what I'd choose for this.

I don't usually write reviews, but I have a hunch that the creator of this masterpiece is going to read this. I'm not going to lie—I was a little disappointed that the game ended so quickly, but... I have to admit that it's actually better this way; it was a good decision. It’s one of the best games I’ve played to date simply because it’s fun—it’s not a game with a complex story or convoluted mechanics. You have your tools, you decide how to use them, and you play however you like. Without a doubt, a great experience. This developer or team of developers deserves a thousand compliments for creating something so simple and efficient. Right now I’m unemployed, but when I go back to work, I won’t hesitate to buy the support pack. Endless thanks to the team. Fun fact: I played through the whole game in one go because I got temporarily banned from CS2 due to kernel issues on my computer (HP Victus 15 running Kubuntu).
